hooks.text: Ten days after a bomb exploded in his garden, Gandhi died.
Why did Mahatma Gandhi refuse guards even after a failed bombing?
Gandhi survived five assassination attempts before the final walk in 1948.

title: Why Did Gandhi Refuse Guards Before His Assassination? 🤯
description: On January 30, 1948, Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated in New Delhi. Despite surviving a bombing just ten days prior, he walked to his prayers without a single guard.

beats.text: Ten days after a bomb exploded in his garden, Gandhi died.
beats.visual: photograph of Mahatma Gandhi walking toward his garden, 1947

beats.text: Many believe the famous pacifist was simply caught off guard.
beats.visual: photograph of the gardens at Birla House in New Delhi, 1948

beats.text: In reality, the seventy-eight-year-old leader had already survived five prior attempts.
beats.visual: portrait of Mahatma Gandhi wearing a traditional shawl, 1940s

beats.text: He strictly refused armed guards, leaning only on his grandnieces for support.
beats.visual: photograph of the stone footsteps leading to the prayer lawn, 1948

beats.text: An American diplomat tackled the killer, but the tragedy began.
beats.visual: photograph of a Beretta Model 1934 semi-automatic pistol

beats.text: He died because he refused protection after a bomb exploded in his garden.
beats.visual: photograph of the Raj Ghat memorial site in New Delhi
